grammar_notes.text: The suffix -re is used to indicate 'he is'.
The word 'mo' means good, and when combined with the suffix '-re', it forms 'more', meaning 'good at'.
-re is an existential suffix indicating 'there are'.
The suffix -to is used to denote 'little' or diminutive forms, as seen in he-to (boy) and yi-to (girl). This pattern can be applied to other nouns to create diminutives.
The suffix -ne is a questioning mode marker, as seen in Morene (are you good?). This can be applied to other stems to form questions.
The phrase ya-suuke-re translates to 'I love you' or 'you are my home'. This structure can be used with other stems to express similar sentiments.
